title: Single-Nucleus RNA Sequencing from Fresh-Frozen Human Heart Tissue
author: Natalia-Del Pilar Vanegas
materials: Keep all reagents and samples at 4 °C. Use wide-bore tips at every pipetting step. Start with 50 mg of pulverized frozen tissue (cryopulverized under liquid nitrogen). Maintaining the tissue frozen until lysis is critical. Add 200 µL lysis buffer to the pulverized tissue. Homogenize with cordless pellet pestle motor for ~30 seconds. Avoid over-homogenization. Add remaining 800 µL lysis buffer (total 1 mL). Incubate on ice for exactly 1 minute. Prolonged lysis in the presence of IGEPAL and Digitonin risks nuclear lysis. Filter lysate through a 30 µm cell strainer to remove large myofibrillar debris and undigested tissue fragments, which are abundant in heart tissue. Vortex filtered lysate briefly (10 sec) to dissociate loose aggregates before centrifugation. Centrifuge at 500 × g, 3 min, 4 °C. Discard supernatant completely. Resuspend pellet in 1 mL wash buffer using gentle wide-bore pipetting (5–6 strokes). Centrifuge at 300 × g, 5 min, 4 °C. Discard supernatant. Repeat once (2 washes total). The lower g-force in wash steps favors nuclei recovery over debris pellet down. RNase Inhibitor in the wash buffer protects nuclear RNA throughout these steps. Resuspend pellet in 1 mL wash buffer. Add 10 µL DNase I (1 U/µL). Mix by inverting the tube 2–3× only — do not vortex, as this disrupts nuclei. Incubate on ice for 5 minutes. DNase I treatment is especially critical for heart tissue. Stop DNase I activity by adding 10 µL 50 mM EDTA. EDTA chelates the Mg²⁺ cofactor required for DNase I catalysis. Filter suspension through a 20 µm strainer to remove residual debris and any remainingaggregates not dissolved by DNase I treatment. Centrifuge at 300 × g, 5 min, 4 °C. Discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 1 mL 0.25 M sucrose buffer. Centrifuge at 500 × g, 5 min, 4 °C. The sucrose cushion provides density-based separation. Discard the top layer carefully. Retain the pellet. Resuspend nuclei in an appropriate volume of Wash Buffer. Assess nuclei by microscopy before counting: nuclei from heart tissue should appear round and uniform with minimal debris. If significant clumping persists, perform an additional DNase I treatment (5 min on ice) and re-filter through 20 µm. Count nuclei using Countess III FL with Propidium Iodide staining. Target: ≥ 500,000 intact nuclei at ≥ 70% viability for fixation input.

steps.title: Prepare Buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary buffers for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Lysis Buffer (use 1 mL per 50 mg tissue).
Prepare Wash / Resuspension Buffer by dissolving 4.28 g sucrose in 50 mL WashBuffer (0.25 M Sucrose Buffer) and keep cold.

steps.title: Fix Nuclei
steps.instruction: Perform fixation of nuclei and verify count.

substeps.instruction: Perform fixation according to Demonstrated Protocol CG000478 (Fixation of Cells & Nuclei for Chromium Fixed RNA Profiling).
Recount fixed nuclei using Countess II FL with Ethidium Homodimer-1.

steps.title: Hybridize Nuclei
steps.instruction: Prepare and execute the hybridization mix for each sample.

substeps.instruction: Combine the fixed nuclei suspension with the sample-specific Probe Barcode set (LHS + RHS probe pairs; Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Fixed RNA Human Transcriptome Probe Set, PN-1000420/1000456).
Add Post-Hybridization (Post-Hyb) Buffer and wash to remove unbound probes.
Recount fixed nuclei using Countess II FL with Ethidium Homodimer-1.
Resuspend each hybridized sample in the volume specified for pooling.

steps.title: Pool and Prepare Samples
steps.instruction: Pool hybridized samples and adjust concentration for loading.

substeps.instruction: Pool up to 16 hybridized samples in equal proportions (consult Pooling Workbook CG000565 for equalization strategies).
Centrifuge pooled sample at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend in GEM loading volume specified in CG000527.
Count pooled nuclei with Countess III FL.
Adjust to target input concentration for Chromium Chip Q loading.

steps.title: Generate GEMs and Libraries
steps.instruction: Perform GEM generation, library construction, and sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Proceed immediately to GEM generation per CG000527 on Chromium X/iX.
Construct Gene Expression libraries by PCR amplification using Dual Index Kit TT Set A.
Assess library quality with Bioanalyzer (expected size ~200–300 bp).
Sequence on an Illumina platform using the following cycle configuration: 28 cycles (R1) + 10 cycles (i7) + 10 cycles (i5) + 90 cycles (R2).
Target ≥ 15,000 reads per nucleus per sample.

steps.title: Process Sequencing Data
steps.instruction: Process raw sequencing data using the cellranger multi pipeline via 10x Genomics Cloud Analysis.

substeps.instruction: Upload FASTQ files using the Cloud CLI tool.
Assign the library type as 'Flex Gene Expression' for each FASTQ set in the project interface.
Select all FASTQ files from a single GEM well and click 'Create New Analysis'.

Specify the following parameters: (i) reference genome — human GRH38-2024-A; (ii) probe set reference matching the kit used (PN-1000420 or PN-1000456); (iii) the Probe Barcode ID assigned to each sample during hybridization.

steps.title: Perform Quality Control
steps.instruction: Review the web_summary.html interactive per-sample QC report.

substeps.instruction: Review estimated number of nuclei, median genes per nucleus, sequencing saturation, fraction of reads confidently mapped to the probe set, and the knee plot for cell calling.
Flag samples with saturation < 50% or median genes < 1,000 for re-sequencing.

steps.title: Visualize and Export Data
steps.instruction: Use Loupe Browser and export matrices for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Open the sample_cloupe.cloupe file in Loupe Browser for interactive visualization of UMAP projections, unsupervised clusters, and per-gene expression.
Utilize the filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ (barcodes.tsv.gz, features.tsv.gz, matrix.mtx.gz) as primary input for downstream analysis in R(Seurat) or Python (Scanpy/AnnData).
